record.context_brief: Euler equations with sources and sinks
record.original_question: Find a variational, ideally geodesic, formulation for the motion of an ideal incompressible fluid in a fixed domain with sources and sinks. The formulation should specify how boundary flux data, transported vorticity entering through source parts of the boundary, exterior forcing, and any fluid-memory effects enter the action principle for Euler-type motion.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Find a variational (preferably geodesic) formulation describing the motion of an ideal fluid in a fixed domain M containing sources and sinks. What is the correct formulation of the variational problem: should one take into account the exterior forces and/or the “memory” of the fluid? For example, consider the case of a horizontal pipe with a fluid entering at one end and exiting at the other end. Such problems have a long history. On the one hand, as any mechanical system, fluid motions should obey some least action principle, see [5]. On the other hand, the energy of the fluid in the pipe may not be conserved since, depending on the boundary conditions, it could be supplied or drained at the two ends. For instance, in addition to the equations (1.1) and the initial condition v(0), the full system of the Euler-type equations in the 2D setting would have to include as data two other items: the function v · n describing the normal component of the velocity v on the penetrable boundary, as well as the vorticity function ω := curl v defined on the source part of the boundary through which the fluid is supplied. (Since vorticity is transported by the flow, this data will be sufficient to define it for all times, see [52, 146, 143, 134].) V. Yudovich used such data to formulate a stability criterion for a steady pipe flow in 2D, which may hint at the appropriate boundary conditions needed to obtain a variational formulation, see [146, 148]. We should add that for a “dual” problem involving a fixed amount of fluid in a domain with a dynamic boundary its Hamiltonian formulation is described in [84]. 3

artifact.category_tag: geometric hydrodynamics with sources and sinks
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in geometric hydrodynamics. Related geodesic/groupoid formulations have been developed for generalized flows, multiphase fluids, and vortex sheets (e.g., Izosimov–Khesin), but these works treat volume-preserving dynamics and do not provide a variational/geodesic formulation that incorporates penetrable-boundary flux data, transported boundary vorticity, exterior forcing, and fluid memory in the source/sink setting. No publication establishing a complete variational/geodesic principle for the Euler equations with sources and sinks was found.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of generalized fluid flows (Izosimov–Khesin)
status_evidence.snippet: Describes generalized flows, multiphase fluids and vortex sheets via Lie groupoid geodesics for the L2-metric; focuses on volume-preserving dynamics, not source/sink boundaries.
status_evidence.claim: Related groupoid/geodesic formulations exist for multiphase fluids but do not handle penetrable boundaries with sources and sinks.
